summary: This file implements a collapsible code snippet component for documentation that can display syntax-highlighted code with optional AI-generated explanations. It supports per-line annotations via tooltips (Eli5CodeBlock), a summary explanation panel (Eli5SummaryBlock), and falls back to Docusaurus's standard CodeBlock when no annotations exist. The component intelligently detects the code language from props, filenames, or React children, maps it to styling variants with corresponding icons, and handles variable substitution throughout.

explanations.27: These imports load additional language definitions into Prism's singleton—without them, syntax highlighting for languages beyond Prism's default bundle (like TypeScript, Python, PHP, Bash) wouldn't work.
explanations.54: This function recursively searches through React child elements to extract the language from a className attribute like 'language-javascript', needed when the language isn't explicitly passed as a prop.
explanations.83: This map normalizes various language names and file extensions (like 'py', 'python', 'ts', 'typescript') down to canonical variants ('python', 'ts') that are used for styling and icon selection.
explanations.144: This interface defines the shape of icon metadata—which CSS class to apply, which icon set ID to use, and the accessibility label for that icon.
explanations.150: This object maps language variants to their visual representation: CSS classes for styling, Iconify icon identifiers, and accessible labels.
explanations.334: This custom hook manages the 'copy to clipboard' functionality, tracking whether a copy succeeded and auto-dismissing the success state after 1 second.
explanations.336: This ref stores a timeout ID so the component can clean it up if the component unmounts while a timeout is pending, preventing memory leaks.
explanations.357: This flag tracks whether the component has mounted on the client; it's needed because the tooltip uses createPortal to render into document.body, which doesn't exist during server-side rendering.
explanations.358: This ref object stores button DOM elements keyed by line number, so the tooltip can calculate its position relative to each annotation badge.
explanations.376: This memoized value looks up the Prism language grammar for the current language; it falls back to plaintext or a generic grammar if the language isn't found, preventing crashes.
explanations.380: useTokenize is called with Prism's token data to get properly-tokenized lines for rendering; unlike naive string splitting, it handles multi-line tokens (like block comments) correctly.
explanations.385: useTokenize sometimes appends a synthetic empty line at the end if the code ends with a newline; this memoized logic removes it so line numbers stay in sync with the eli5 annotations object.
explanations.394: This callback computes the screen position where the tooltip should appear (above and right-aligned to the badge button) using getBoundingClientRect().
explanations.415: This event listener handler is wrapped in useCallback so it can be cleanly added and removed in the cleanup function; it ensures the tooltip stays glued to its badge as the page scrolls.
explanations.424: This line grabs the explanation text for the currently active line number from the eli5 object, or null if no line is active.
explanations.443: The map function iterates over tokenized lines (each line is an array of tokens with type info and content), converting each to a rendered line div with syntax highlighting spans.
explanations.462: This callback ref stores the DOM button element for this line number in the badgeRefs object, so positionTooltip() can later retrieve it to calculate the tooltip's position.
explanations.524: useId() generates a unique ID for the summary disclosure's aria-controls relationship, ensuring the button and content div are properly linked for accessibility.
explanations.589: This memoized value safely parses the eli5json prop (a JSON string injected by the build plugin) into a JavaScript object; if parsing fails, it returns null to gracefully degrade.
explanations.613: This memoized logic implements a priority chain: first check the explicit lang prop, then search React children for a language-xyz className, finally infer from filename extension, with 'plaintext' as the ultimate fallback.
explanations.636: Variable substitution is applied to the code string; this replaces placeholders like %%variableName%% with actual values before passing to Prism for syntax highlighting.
explanations.642: Variable substitution for React children wraps substituted values in VarToken components, which typically add visual styling (like underlines) to indicate user-provided values.
explanations.650: This memoized logic chooses which code renderer to use: the custom Eli5CodeBlock if line-by-line annotations exist, Docusaurus's CodeBlock for plain syntax highlighting, or raw children as fallback.
explanations.668: This checks if the filename matches Docker-related patterns (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yaml, etc.) to select Docker-specific styling and icon.
explanations.684: This determines the styling variant key by checking (in order): an explicit variant prop, special cases for Docker/Docusaurus files, the language-to-variant map, or 'none' as a default.
explanations.692: This looks up the CSS class for the chosen variant from the styles object; for example, styles.variant_python would style a Python code block differently than styles.variant_js.
explanations.699: This chooses a display title for the header, preferring an explicit title, then filename, then the language name in uppercase, with 'Snippet' as a final fallback.
